title: Optimization Advisory Playbook & Routing Matrix for Enterprise Requests
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create a repeatable playbook and routing matrix to triage incoming optimization and advisory requests (batching/caching knobs, quantization recommendations, routing policies). Goal: reduce time-to-first-response for enterprise customers, ensure consistent prioritization, and provide clear handoffs between Support, Solutions Engineering, Product, and Runtime Engineering teams. This ticket will produce a written playbook, machine-readable scoring rubric, sample routing rules for the Console and intake forms, and a pilot rollout plan for top enterprise accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook document drafted with intake channels, triage rubric, templated responses, and escalation paths
Scoring rubric produced as CSV/JSON-ready table (fields and weighting) and validated on 50 historical advisory requests
Routing matrix mapping score ranges and request types to teams/SLAs (self-serve, advisory queue, SE engagement, eng change) is approved by stakeholders
Console intake form prototypes created with required fields and suggested defaults for enterprise customers
Pilot plan defined (selection criteria for accounts, metrics, success thresholds) and signed off by Support and Solutions Eng
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: interviewed Support (Maya Patel) and Solutions Eng leads. Common pain: ambiguous requests labeled 'performance' that actually represent feature wishlist vs urgent SLO regression.
2026-03-04 - Decision: triage rubric must explicitly separate 'operational' (latency/cost regressions) vs 'optimization advisory' (best-effort tuning) vs 'product change' (engine/runtime work).
2026-03-06 - Action: asked Observability team (ENG-4389) for aggregated request metadata: most common model families, average token sizes, and % of requests from Dedicated customers.

2026-03-09 - Drafted scoring fields: customer_tier, workload_type (chat/generation/embeddings/rerank), observed_latency_delta, cost_sensitivity, security_constraints, regulatory_scope, historical_impact. Weighting proposed: customer_tier 30%, workload_impact 25%, latency_impact 20%, security 15%, cost 10%.

2026-03-11 - SolEng review: suggested adding 'business-critical pathway' flag and auto-escalate if customer reports P0 production outage. Also recommended defaulting enterprise accounts to 'advisory queue' rather than self-serve.
2026-03-13 - Legal/Compliance input: Private/VPC requests with audit/KMS requirements should be flagged and routed to Privacy & Security for pre-engagement checklists before engineering work begins.
2026-03-14 - Next steps: build intake prototype in Console (PM+Design), create CSV of historical requests for rubric validation, schedule pilot with top 10 enterprise customers in April.
notes: We will prioritize building the rubric such that it can be run retrospectively against historical tickets to estimate time-savings and false positives. The Console intake must support attachments (logs, perf traces) and an optional KV cache snapshots link. Pilot success metrics: mean time to first meaningful response <= 24h, correct routing rate >= 85%, and reduction in ad-hoc SE engagements by 30% over 8 weeks.
example_triage_scenarios: Scenario A: Enterprise customer reports 2x token latency spike after model upgrade -> score high on latency_impact and customer_tier -> route to Reliability SRE + runtime eng for immediate investigation (SLA: 4h initial response).

Scenario B: Startup asks for quantization guidance for cost reduction on non-sensitive data -> low security constraint, low latency impact -> route to self-serve docs + scheduled advisory office hours (SE).

Scenario C: Financial customer requests on-prem quantization profile and KMS integration -> high security/regulatory flag -> route to Privacy & Security pre-engagement and Solutions Eng for PS/Professional Services scoping.
